about: The open-source projects AMAL's code, skills and tools come from or use. Checked every 24 hours (AMAL_TASKS.md): newest release or commit, licence, what changed that matters to AMAL. 'use' says how AMAL uses it: built-in (code copied into AMAL), toolbox (capability or skill in AMAL-toolbox), harness (a selectable agent harness), external (a program AMAL drives), research (watched, not installed), waiting (the owner linked it and it is not in AMAL yet - what it would be for is in 'why'), set-aside (in the Python app (0.16) or asked for before the rebuild of 2026-10-29 and not carried over; his word brings it back), dropped (the owner dropped it - the date and his reason are in 'why'; never checked, never brought back by itself). 'pinned' is the commit or release tag AMAL tested; empty = follows the newest. crates/amald/src/sources.rs checks them all once a day (Settings › Sources). Everything the owner ever linked or named for this project is here, so nothing he asked for is forgotten: a link he gives gets a line the same day.

sources.why: owner 2026-11-13: 'get RTK and Headroom running on all machines and that should be an AMAL thing users can install'. One Rust program that shortens what commands print before a model reads it. In AMAL since 2026-11-14: Settings > Setup installs it (Mac: brew rtk-ai/tap/rtk-oss, the Apache-2.0 edition; Windows: winget rtk-ai.rtk, which also carries its BUSL-1.1 engine - free to use, not to resell), and a job's `run` asks `rtk rewrite` and runs the command through it when RTK has a filter for it (tools.rs rtk_form; AMAL_RTK=0 turns it off). Its telemetry is off unless turned on. Not measured yet: one code job with and without (calls.jsonl)
sources.pinned: v1.2.0 (2026-11-08) read; installed by brew / winget at its current version

sources.why: owner 2026-11-13 (and 2026-10-13: it was in the Python app). A compression layer between an agent and its model. In AMAL since 2026-11-13: its two rule-based crushers, in Rust inside the loop (crates/amal-core/src/crush.rs) - a command's long output keeps its errors with the lines around them, its stack traces, a few distinct warnings, its summary and its end where it kept only its last 8,000 characters; a long JSON list keeps its first and last rows and the rows with errors. No Python and no second program on the path (rule 9). Not taken: its proxy, its learned compressor (Kompress), fetching the left-out rows back, its MCP server - to measure against the built-in rules on the same job before any of them is added. The Mac has a ~/.headroom folder from the Python app

owner 2026-11-13: 'are we using omni route?' - no; AMAL routes with its own pool (pool.rs, llm.rs). OmniRoute is a local gateway (Node, 127.0.0.1:20128/v1, OpenAI-style) over some 350 providers with fall-back chains and RTK + Caveman compression - the same idea as 9router, which the Python app had. Much of its free list is other tools' subscriptions signed in through it, which is each service's terms and his call per account; the routes that are plainly free API tiers AMAL's free-model search can list itself. If tried: as one more route in the pool, bound to this machine only, never in place of the pool
